subject: Cerebra Dedicated: sizing, burst credits, and autoscale governance
messages:

Cc: Manny Lopez <manny.lopez@cerebra.ai>

Subject: Dedicated capacity for Q1 launch - burst and billing questions

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. We're mapping out the Dedicated sizing for our Q1 product launch and need to lock down a few things before procurement can issue a PO:

- How does Redwood handle ephemeral burst above committed GPUs (pricing and guaranteed credits)?
- What autoscale policies would you recommend for low-latency chat workloads (mostly 2k token span, heavy concurrency spikes)?
- Any constraints around cross-region failover or preemption we should know for SLAs?

Attached is a rough forecast (3-week ramp) and the model types we expect to serve. Can you provide a recommended commit + burst profile and an ops runbook we can include in our SOW?

We need procurement guidance by next Friday (2026-10-27) to hit our timeline.

Best,
Elena
--

Head of Platform
Cerebra AI
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@cerebra.ai>
Cc: Manny Lopez <manny.lopez@cerebra.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for Q1 launch - burst and billing questions

Elena — thanks for the clear summary. High level answers and a recommended commit profile below; detailed workbook attached (Cerebra_Dedicated_Modeling.xlsx) and a short PDF with policy options.

Summary (recommendation):
- Baseline reserved capacity: 8 GPUs (NVIDIA A10-equivalent) sized for steady-state throughput.
- Shoulder reserve (soft committed buffer): 4 GPUs — billed at a discounted reserved rate, available to absorb short spikes.
- Ephemeral burst pool: up to 12 GPUs (preemptible/ephemeral) for transient spikes beyond shoulder; burst usage charged at usage rates with monthly burst-credit allotment.
- Guaranteed monthly burst credits: propose 1,200 GPU-hours included (can be negotiated in SOW).

Autoscale policy suggestion for chat-heavy workloads:
- Scale-up trigger: sustained GPU utilization > 70% for 30s or queue depth > 60 requests for 60s.
- Scale-down: maintain for 120s after below-threshold; include minimum hold of 5 minutes to avoid oscillation.
- Prewarm window: 5 minutes for predicted scheduled ramps (customer-initiated or forecast API).

Operational constraints and fallbacks:
- Cross-region failover: supported but will count against reserved pool in target region; recommend reserving small standby capacity in secondary region if cross-region SLA is required.
- Preemption: ephemeral GPUs are preemptible; we commit to draining in-flight requests and failing over to nearest compatible model variant if eviction occurs.
- SLA: Reserved capacity covered by SLA (99.9) — ephemeral pool is best-effort.

Next steps: I can draft the SOW language around "burst credits" and attach the ops runbook. Do you want guaranteed monthly burst hours included in the initial contract or as an add-on clause? Also, what's the procurement timeline and who will sign the SOW?

Attachments: Cerebra_Dedicated_Modeling.xlsx; redwood-dedicated-burst-options.pdf

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>

Subject: FWD: Cerebra Dedicated: sizing, burst credits, and autoscale governance

Team — forwarding Elena's ask and my proposed profile above. Key asks from procurement: they want a clear SOW line for "guaranteed monthly burst credits" and firm autoscale governance so finance can model committed costs. Can ops validate feasibility and provide SKU mapping + a quick cost delta for 1,200 included burst hours vs pay-as-you-go?

A few specifics we need confirmation on from infra/ops:
- Map the recommended "A10-equivalent" to our current fleet SKUs in us-west-2 and confirm availability for ephemeral bursts.
- Eviction behavior: how long to drain KV caches / in-flight tokens on preemption for long-context models (2k tokens)? Any additional latency impact to expect during failover?
- Crediting cadence: do we credit burst hours daily or monthly? What fraction of unused burst credits can roll over?
- Autoscale knobs: confirm safe thresholds (I suggested 70% util / 30s uplift); provide guidance if we should raise/lower thresholds for multi-tenant noisy neighbors.

I'll add the proposed SOW language once you confirm. Hoping to have numbers back by end of day so I can push SOW to procurement Friday morning.

Thanks — Ben
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Cc: ops_capacity@redwood.inference
Date: 2026-10-20T15:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Cerebra Dedicated: sizing, burst credits, and autoscale governance

Ben/Monica — quick ops read and recommendations below. I ran this with capacity planning and runtime teams; attaching the small SKU mapping (capacity-mapping-v2.csv).

Feasibility/ops notes:
- SKU mapping: A10-equivalent maps to our T4-heavy slab for compatibility; availability in us-west-2 for ephemeral pool is feasible but limited in mornings (local peak). Recommend we place ephemeral pool on mixed-sku (A10 + A2) to increase headroom and avoid single-sku contention.
- Eviction/drain model: runtime will attempt graceful drain for 60s on preemption for typical 2k contexts; if eviction happens during sampling-heavy workloads we expect tail latency spikes ~200-400ms while failover to variant occurs. Mitigation: enable small per-request retry with jitter + fallback to a compact model variant.
- Crediting: monthly allotment with 3-month rollover of unused credits (cap at 25% of monthly allotment). Billing will show burst usage separately; finance prefers monthly reconciliation.
- Autoscale knobs: the suggested 70% / 30s is a reasonable starting point. For multi-tenant noisy neighbors, increase scale-up trigger to 75% and use more conservative prewarm (7m). For Cerebra — since they are latency-sensitive — keep 70% but add a hard cap on concurrent queued requests to protect p95 latency.
- SLA language: confirm reserved capacity SLA 99.9; add fallback clause to route to hosted models with equivalent semantics if Dedicated pool is exhausted (customer opt-in).

Operational asks for SOW:
- Include guaranteed monthly burst hours (we can do 1,200 GPU-hours as proposed).
- Define credit rollover and reconciliation cadence (monthly statement, 3-month rollup cap at 25%).
- Maintenance windows: request 12 hours' advance notice for scheduled maintenance; emergency maintenance to be escalated with 2-hour notice where possible.

I'll hand off final cost delta for 1,200 GPU-hours vs pay-as-you-go in a separate note (ops_capacity will produce). Once we have costs, Ben you can finalize SOW language.

-Karthik
